title: Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess Demo
provenance: Reported by udance4ever (highball-db#69, 2026-09-16), Apple M1, macOS 26.7, Highball 0.9.19, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r3, D3DMetal, with DXMT and DXVK tried too, rated 1 of 5 at first: in every mode the game stops with its unsupported graphics card error, naming AtomicInt64OnDescriptorHeapResourceSupported (screenshot). udance4ever again (highball-db#69, 2026-09-18): the same with D3DMetal 3 on macOS 27. udance4ever again (highball-db#69, 2026-11-15), Apple M1, macOS 27.2, the Wine 11 engine x64-crossover26.3-r32 (D3DMetal 4.0 beta 3 by the Metal HUD), D3DMetal, with HB_TSSHIM_ATOMIC64=1 and HB_X87SIDECAR=1 in the environment's variables (log): the demo gets past the check, compiles its shaders and reaches gameplay, where the scene draws as black silhouettes over a flat pale grey ground and sky, at about 30 fps at 1920x1080 (screenshot). The report now rates it 2 of 5. A DualSense wasn't recognised with Steam Input on or off, where the same controller worked in the Onimusha: Way of the Sword demo, and an XInput controller worked. Not verified by the maintainer. udance4ever again (highball-db#69, 2026-11-17): the same picture on the Wine 11 engine r33 (D3DMetal 3), and on r32 the character draws right once it moves while its surroundings don't (screenshot). After the environment went to r33 the DualSense worked with Steam Input, and it kept working back on r32.
notes: Capcom's RE Engine, DirectX 12. On an M1 it stops at start with an unsupported graphics card error, because D3DMetal answers no to the game's check for 64-bit atomics on descriptor heap resources (D3D12 OPTIONS11), the same check as the Onimusha: Way of the Sword demo and PRAGMATA Sketchbook. On an M4 D3DMetal 3 already answers yes (measured here 2026-10-14 with a probe). On Highball's Wine 11 engines (r25 or later) the variable HB_TSSHIM_ATOMIC64=1 makes Highball's DirectX 12 layer answer yes, and with it a player reached gameplay on an M1, but the scene draws wrongly, black silhouettes over a flat pale ground (highball-db#69, r32 with D3DMetal 4.0 beta 3). D3DMetal 3 on the Wine 11 engine r33 draws it the same way, so it isn't D3DMetal 4's beta. The character draws right once it moves, its surroundings don't. Whether that comes from the game using a feature D3DMetal says the M1 doesn't have, or from something else, isn't known. No recipe sets the variable for this demo, so a player adds it to the environment's variables by hand, where it reaches every game in that environment.

knownIssues.symptom: Unsupported graphics card error at start, naming AtomicInt64OnDescriptorHeapResourceSupported, then the game quits (M1, the same in D3DMetal, DXMT and DXVK mode)
knownIssues.cause: D3DMetal reports AtomicInt64OnDescriptorHeapResourceSupported as false on M1 chips, and RE Engine requires it
knownIssues.fix: the player's way past it: a Wine 11 engine (r25 or later) with HB_TSSHIM_ATOMIC64=1 in the environment's variables, which has Highball's layer in front of D3DMetal answer yes (highball-db#69). The game then draws wrongly, see below. No recipe sets it for this demo

knownIssues.symptom: In gameplay the scene draws as black silhouettes over a flat pale grey ground and sky (M1, Wine 11 r32 with D3DMetal 4.0 beta 3, HB_TSSHIM_ATOMIC64=1). The same on r33 with D3DMetal 3, and the character draws right once it moves
A DualSense isn't recognised in the game, with Steam Input on or off (M1)
knownIssues.cause: not diagnosed. The same controller worked in the Onimusha: Way of the Sword demo, also RE Engine
knownIssues.fix: an XInput controller worked (highball-db#69). Later the DualSense worked after the environment moved to r33, and kept working back on r32
